title: x-nav: learning end-to-end cross-embodiment navigation for mobile robots
core_idea: Introduce X-Nav, a two-stage framework that first trains multiple expert policies with deep reinforcement learning using privileged observations on a variety of randomly generated robot embodiments, then distills those experts into a single general policy via navigation action chunking and transformer-based imitation learning (nav-act) that maps visual and proprioceptive observations to low-level control for deployment across diverse wheeled and quadrupedal robots.
tldr: Proposes a two-stage method to learn one unified end-to-end navigation policy that generalizes across diverse robot embodiments by distilling many RL experts into a transformer-based controller using navigation action chunking.
